subject: Re: Limitation of liability — exclusions for indirect losses and lost profits
messages:
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Ellis <j.ellis@acmeanalytics.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-18T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: MSA redlines — liability carve-outs and examples (attached)

Jordan — attaching our clean redline (v3) with a short summary in the spreadsheet. High level notes: we accepted three of Acme's minor edits but kept our position on Limitation of Liability and consequential loss exclusions. Key open points are: (1) whether lost profits are excluded as indirect; (2) whether data loss qualifies for the confidentiality/data breach carve-out; and (3) cap sizing (we propose 3x fees or $1,000,000 floor).

Requested next steps: can you confirm Acme's negotiators for legal (in-house) + procurement so we can target a final by next Wednesday? If helpful, I pasted proposed compromise language below (quick reference).

— Proposed compromise for exclusion carve-out (clean):
"Neither party shall be liable to the other for any indirect, special, incidental, consequential or punitive damages (including, but not limited to, loss of profits, loss of business, loss of data or loss of goodwill), except to the extent such damages arise from: (a) a party's gross negligence or willful misconduct; (b) a proven breach of the confidentiality obligations; or (c) a party's failure to pay amounts due under this Agreement."

— Proposed cap language (clean):
"Except for liability arising from (a) breach of confidentiality, (b) gross negligence or willful misconduct, (c) a party's indemnity obligations, or (d) liability required by applicable law, each party's aggregate liability under this Agreement shall not exceed the greater of (i) three (3) times the fees paid or payable by Customer to Redwood under the applicable Order Form in the twelve (12) months preceding the event giving rise to the claim and (ii) One Million US Dollars (US$1,000,000)."

Attachments: Acme_MSA_Redline_v3.pdf (redline), redline_summary.xlsx (two-sheet summary: open items + suggested compromise wording).

Thanks,
Rishi

Subject: Re: MSA redlines — liability carve-outs and examples (attached)

Thanks Rishi — got the materials. A few immediate reactions from Acme legal/counsel:
1) Lost profits: we view certain lost profits (reasonably foreseeable revenue loss caused by prolonged downtime) as recoverable and subject to a higher cap carve-out. Our redline proposes a carve-out that keeps "lost profits" recoverable where they arise from Redwood's gross negligence or material breach of service-level commitments.
2) Data loss: Acme insists that data loss resulting from Redwood's failure to maintain reasonable security controls be recoverable and not treated as purely consequential.
3) Cap floor: $1M floor is reasonable but we want a higher multiplier (5x fees) for strategic accounts or a dollar-capped exception for breaches of security/confidentiality at $5M.

I'll have Kathy circulate a marked-up version by EOD with specific language and examples (e.g., an actual example draft: lost profits = direct lost revenue from missed renewals attributable to a documented 48-hour outage). Also copying procurement so they can confirm credit terms.

Jordan Ellis
General Counsel (interim)
Acme Analytics
j.ellis@acmeanalytics.com

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-18T13:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: internal — Acme MSA liability points (prep for call)

Looping in internal notes for the call with Acme at 3pm PT. Quick play-by-play: 
- On lost profits: keep high-level exclusion for "loss of profits" as indirect, but agree to a narrow carve-out where lost profits may be recoverable if tied to: (i) a documented SLA failure that Redwood failed to cure after written notice; and (ii) demonstrable, invoiced lost business directly linked to the outage (e.g., canceled contracts within 90 days). Example drafting below.
- On data loss: classify as direct only when it results from an unauthorized access attributable to Redwood's gross negligence or a verified data breach; otherwise, treat as consequential where downstream reputational impacts are excluded.
- Cap sizing: propose a flexible matrix in negotiation: Standard customers = 3x fees / $1M floor; Strategic customers (defined in an SOW) = 5x fees / $3M floor; security/confidentiality breaches carry a separate higher sub-cap up to $5M but only for proven regulatory fines and forensic remediation costs (not reputational damages).

Draft sample clause for lost profits carve-out (internal):
"Notwithstanding the foregoing exclusions for indirect and consequential damages, Customer may recover lost profits resulting directly from Redwood's material breach of the Service Level Agreement, provided that: (i) Customer notifies Redwood in writing within ten (10) days of the outage; (ii) Customer submits contemporaneous evidence of the lost revenue; and (iii) such lost profits are limited to revenues Customer would have received from contracts in force during the ninety (90) day period following the date of the relevant outage and are subject to the overall liability cap set forth herein."

Marissa — please prepare a short two-slide summary with these examples and a suggested redline to circulate at the call. Rishi — if Acme pushes $5M immediately, be ready to offer the strategic account matrix instead of a flat $5M floor.

Laura
Laura Bennett
VP, Legal Operations | Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwood.ai

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>

Date: 2026-10-18T17:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MSA redlines — compromise proposal ahead of 3pm call

Jordan — thanks for the early feedback. Attached is a short one-pager that summarizes Redwood's compromise ahead of the call; highlights below so we can streamline the discussion: 
1) Lost profits: carve-out allowed only where lost profits are: (a) tied to a documented SLA failure that Redwood materially breached and failed to cure; and (b) supported by contemporaneous revenue evidence. Limitation: capped by the standard liability cap unless the account is designated "Strategic" in the Order Form. Example given in the one-pager.
2) Data loss: will be direct and recoverable when caused by verified unauthorized access or failure of Redwood's security obligations; remediation costs and regulatory fines recoverable up to $5M sub-cap for such events, but not reputational damages or speculative future earnings.
3) Cap matrix: propose the three-tier matrix Laura outlined (Standard / Strategic / Security breach sub-cap).

If Acme is comfortable with this framework, we will convert these bullets into redline language on the call and attempt to finalize. If you want the exact redline pre-call, Kathy, please let me know and we'll push an updated PDF immediately.

Best,
Rishi
